note: Registry of pre-auth surfaces for the enumeration-boundary parity harness (test/example/test/example_web/enumeration_parity_test.exs). A row with state parity proves ONLY the listed compare dimensions, for ONE request issued for an existing identity and for an unknown identity, and nothing else (not timing, not repeat attempts, not locked or unconfirmed accounts). The harness runs in the example host, a hand-maintained copy of the generated host that already drifts from the generated templates; only install_smoke proves a generated host. States: parity (must compare same), known_divergence (must still differ; fixing the product forces this row to be removed or changed), by_design (documented behaviour is asserted), not_proven (no assertion; blocker cites the file:line that prevents a deterministic probe). The compare lists of the five named rows are pinned in the parity test to the dimensions the published docs rely on (the account-existence rows keep status, redirect, flash and body): a row may list more, never fewer.

surfaces.note: Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One failed attempt (wrong password) for an existing email versus any password for an unknown email, fresh state: no earlier failures, account not locked. Compares the POST status, redirect location, server-side flash map and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. Repeat attempts (lockout), timing and the locked and unconfirmed states are NOT compared; see password-signin-repeat-attempts.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One magic-link request for an existing email versus an unknown email, fresh state. Compares the POST status, redirect location, server-side flash map and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. Email delivery (presence and subject), timing and the library rate limit are NOT compared; see magic-link-rate-limit.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. One reset request submitted through the LiveView form for an existing email versus an unknown email, fresh state. Compares the reported redirect outcome (302), the redirect location, the flash read from the redirect and the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email. NOT compared: response timing (an unknown address costs one dummy hash, an existing one writes a token and delivers an email), email delivery, the rate limit (see password-reset-rate-limit), locked, unconfirmed and enterprise-policy accounts, and the generated host (the example host is a hand-maintained copy; the generated reset page is not compared). The generated host's reset request page is not compared and its defects are tracked by the linked todo.

Identity = the email an anonymous visitor puts in the resend event payload: an existing, still-unconfirmed account versus an address never stored. The resend handler takes its target from the session user and ignores the payload, so this row proves a visitor-supplied identity is ignored, not that an email-keyed resend form exists: no email-keyed resend form exists in the example or in the generated page, and nothing here covers one. One anonymous resend event with the email in its payload, fresh state. Compares the reported redirect outcome (302), the redirect location, the flash read from the redirect (an error asking the visitor to log in), the followed login page body after normalizing only CSRF tokens, request ids and the echoed email, and the number of confirmation tokens created for that email (zero for both). NOT compared: a signed-in visitor's own resend (the session owner's account, not an enumeration channel), response timing, rate limits, the code-entry path, and the generated host (its LiveView confirm flow was repaired in Phase 246 and renders a sign-in-required state in place for an anonymous visitor, which differs from this example's flash-and-redirect; nothing about the generated host is claimed). This row proves a payload email is ignored and is counted separately from the account-existence surfaces (password-signin, magic-link-request, password-reset-request) by the named-surface rule in the parity test; it can never satisfy or substitute for them.

Identity = code kind, not account existence: for a user with an MFA-pending session, one wrong authenticator code (existing) versus one wrong backup code (unknown), each on a freshly enrolled user. Compares the outcome (re-rendered in place, reported as 200), redirect location and the flash message including the remaining-attempts count. The flash is read from the LiveView process state because the view does not render it in its own markup. The body is NOT compared: the authenticator and backup panels differ by design. A pending versus absent MFA session and the lockout outcome are NOT compared. This row is counted separately from the account-existence surfaces (password-signin, magic-link-request, password-reset-request) by the named-surface rule in the parity test and can never satisfy or substitute for them.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account, over repeated attempts. Known divergence, asserted at library level: after the configured lockout threshold of wrong passwords an existing account returns the account_locked error with its own safe message, while an unknown email returns the invalid_credentials error on every attempt because Sigra.Lockout.check/2 returns :ok for a nil user. The example sign-in controller maps every error to one flash, so its HTTP response is the same after the threshold (asserted separately); a host that renders the library safe message would expose the difference. Fixing the library behaviour must change or remove this row.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account (existing = duplicate registration, unknown = new registration). Known divergence, asserted: a new email sets the auto-sign-in trigger (phx-trigger-action on the form, no flash) while a duplicate email re-renders with only an info flash. The difference is inherent to signing a new account in. The duplicate path also returns faster than a new registration (timing oracle, tracked by the linked todo and not compared here). Fixing either must change or remove this row.

Identity = whether the invitee email already has an account. By design the invitation URL is a capability: an anonymous visitor with a valid token sees the same signup branch whether or not the invitee already has an account, and the invitee email shown on the page is part of the capability (normalized as the echoed email). Reading identity parity onto a capability URL is an interpretation. The invalid, expired, revoked, mismatch and signed-in branches are NOT compared.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account. Known divergence, asserted: an unknown email returns an object with the key error while an existing email returns an object with the key options, a real account-existence oracle present in the generated template and in the example host. Fixing it needs a template change and a golden rebless, which is out of scope here. The email-less conditional flow involves no identity and is asserted identical across two anonymous calls. This row is not parity and must not be cited as proof of enumeration safety.

Identity = whether the submitted work email belongs to an account. By design discovery answers per email DOMAIN: two addresses on one connected domain, one registered and one not, get the identical redirect and flash, while a domain without an active connection gets a different answer (the domain, not the user, is what is revealed). The SSO page the redirect lands on is not followed or compared.

Identity = whether the submitted email belongs to an account, under repeated requests. Not proven: the library applies its optional rate limiter only to existing users (an unknown email returns before the limiter runs) and the generated controller swallows the rate_limited result. The example host passes no rate limiter, so the throttle cannot be driven and nothing is compared.
